title: Photosynthesis: how green plants make food
subject: science

objectives.text: Name the leaf, stem and roots and say what each part does, explain photosynthesis using light, water, carbon dioxide, food and oxygen, and describe respiration as the reverse of photosynthesis
successCriteria: I can say the leaf catches light, the stem holds the plant up, and the roots drink in water from the soil
I can explain that light, water and carbon dioxide arrive at the leaf and become food and oxygen
I can describe respiration as breaking down food with oxygen to release energy, making carbon dioxide and water
assessmentPoints: Plant-part answers in the opening activity
Recipe and reverse-process answers in the second and third activities

objectives.text: Explain why plants respire all the time, day and night
successCriteria: I can say that plants take in and give out gases too: they respire all the time, day and night
I can follow the gases moving in and out of the leaf in the day and at night to show respiration never stops
assessmentPoints: Trap discussion in the fourth activity
Breathing answers in the closing practice and the exit ticket

activities.title: Photosynthesis: plants make their own food

differentiation.support: Provide the leaf diagram from the animation so learners can trace the food and oxygen moving into the leaf before describing respiration themselves.

activities.title: A common mistake: plants do not breathe?

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why a plant kept in the dark all night is still respiring even though it cannot photosynthesise.
